title: Claims Adjudication Accounting: Working Out What the Supplement Pays on a Waiting Crossover Line
content:
This is the accounting basis on which the payment on a waiting crossover line under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies is worked out. The line is settled by paying the share of the Medicare cost sharing the plan letter covers, worked out from the amount Medicare approved and from what the line records the policyholder owing, and never from what the provider billed.

### 1. The line settled

The line most recently rendered is settled, and the payment is worked out from its figures.

### 2. The amount the share is taken on

The whole amount recorded as approved is taken.

### 3. The share the plan letter covers

The plan letter's share of the Part B coinsurance is taken.

### 4. The yearly deductible

No yearly deductible is taken, the benefit carrying none.

### 5. The high deductible

On a high-deductible plan letter the supplement pays nothing until the liability the policyholder's paid lines record over the twelve months to date reaches the plan letter's high deductible, and from that point it pays as the plan letter otherwise would. What counts toward that deductible is measured from the claim record: the liability the paid lines of the twelve months to date record is what counts.

### 6. The foreign travel lifetime maximum

Foreign travel emergency care is paid only up to the plan letter's lifetime maximum, what has already been paid on that benefit over the life of the policy being counted against it.

### 7. Putting the figures together

The amount approved less the yearly deductible is taken at the share the plan letter covers, what remains of the high deductible is taken from that share, the figure is rounded to the cent once at the end, it is never more than what remains of the lifetime maximum, and where what remains of the high deductible exceeds the share nothing is paid and the whole of it stands to the policyholder.

### Worked through on hypothetical figures

Take a policy on Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Plan G with two crossover lines waiting on the supplement. The line most recently rendered records an amount approved of 240.00 and the policyholder owing 180.00, and the paid lines of the twelve months to date record liability of 300.00. Nothing has been paid on foreign travel emergency care over the life of the policy.

The line most recently rendered is the line settled. The whole amount recorded as approved is taken, being 240.00. The share taken is that plan letter's share of the Part B coinsurance, being 100 per cent. No yearly deductible is taken.

Taking 240.00 less nothing at 100 per cent gives a share of 240.00. That plan letter carries no high deductible, so nothing of it remains and nothing is taken from the share. What remains of that plan letter's foreign travel lifetime maximum is the whole of it, and 240.00 is well within it.

Rounded to the cent once at the end, the supplement pays 240.00 on the line.
